sources.evidenceExcerpt: Skip to main content HOME DEPARTMENTS RESIDENTS VISITORS BUSINESS I WANT TO EN Facebook Instagram LinkedIn YouTube slide 1 of 1 HOW TO PAY CAMARILLO TROLLEY DIAL-A-RIDE CAMARILLO AIRPORT (OPENS IN NEW WINDOW) METROLINK (OPENS IN NEW WINDOW) HOMERESIDENTSPUBLIC TRANSPORTATIONHOW TO PAY HOW TO PAY CAT offers different forms of payment: Fixed Services - Tap2Ride No cash or bus pass? No problem. Tap2Ride, a contactless fare payment system is now available on CAT bus services. Tap your credit/debit card or phone/watch on the yellow payment reader to board. No app or account needed. Tap2Ride is accepted on the Camarillo Fixed-Route Bus and Camarillo Trolley services only. CAT officially launched Tap2Ride on January 2, 2026. Tap2Ride users can also save money the more they ride CAT bus services. When paying through Tap2Ride, users will be eligible for pay as you go or “fare capping” discounts.

sources.evidenceExcerpt: Skip to main content City of Corvallis Oregon Community Doing Business Government City Services Search form Search Website CORVALLIS TRANSIT SYSTEM ADA Paratransit Cost "Since CTS is fareless, will my BAT Lift rides be fareless, too?" The answer to that question is ...Yes. BAT Lift rides are currently fareless. BAT Lift is the contractor for several different programs but at least two of those programs overlap: The City's ADA Paratransit Service program, and The Benton County Special Transportation Fund (STF) program. (NOTE: While enrollment in the City's program automatically qualifies the rider for the County's program, the reverse is not true. Since the qualification process is different, enrollment in the Benton County STF program does NOT automatically entitle the rider to fareless City ADA paratransit service.) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Three Qualifications

sources.title: Zero-Fare - Mountain Line
sources.evidenceExcerpt: Report a Safety Concern Zero-Fare Mountain Line operates a zero-fare system, meaning you do not have to pay to ride. Since the debut of the Zero-Fare Program in 2015, ridership has increased almost 70 percent. Mountain Line now provides more than 1.5 million rides annually, with 48 percent of riders surveyed reporting they ride the bus more frequently since the Zero-Fare Program began. INCREASING BUS RIDERSHIP BENEFITS US ALL More people riding the bus equates to less traffic congestion, less need for parking facilities and a healthier community, as more people choose active transportation. And, fewer private vehicles on the road results in less air pollution in the Missoula Valley. In short, a robust Mountain Line helps keep Missoula a more livable and prosperous community for everyone. Top 11 Reasons Zero-Fare Matters Public transit benefits us all and helps create a quality community.

sources.evidenceExcerpt: Skip to content Pinellas Suncoast Transit Authority | 'Home' SERVICES RIDER INFO AGENCY NEWS CAREERS CONTACT US Search the site PSTA is There When Gas Prices Spike PSTA is There When Gas Prices Spike THE PRICE AT THE PUMP MAY BE FRIGHTENING, BUT PSTA HAS YOUR BACK! Gas prices in the Tampa Bay Area have surged higher than $4 per gallon, the highest since 2022! And considering insurance prices are at an all-time high, private car owners are certainly feeling the strain. In fact, a recent study show …  the highest since 2022! And considering insurance prices are at an all-time high, private car owners are certainly feeling the strain. In fact, a recent study showed that the average cost of owning a car in Florida is $8,483 per year or more, with Floridians paying the most in hidden car ownership prices nationwide. A rise in gas prices just adds insult to injury. But despite this current rise in fuel pricing, PSTA remains ready to provide some relief. From fixed-route and premium bus services to on-demand services and partnerships with Uber and Lyft, we offer a wide range of alternatives to  … to popular destinations, especially since the launch of our Connected Community Bus Network in October 2025. The Connected Community Bus Network was the largest system redesign in agency history, and focused on providing more frequent service on high-ridership routes, as well as finally giving all routes service seven days a week. Life doesn’t take weekends off, and now neither do any PSTA routes! A rider boarding Route 11. Among our fixed routes are premium services such as SunRunner and Spark. These two services boast a 15-minute frequency during peak hours and provide seamless connections t …  on your vehicle. PSTA provides fare programs to many schools and businesses throughout the county with our UPASS program. Check whether your school or employer already offers you free fares through the UPASS program. If it doesn’t, see if your school or employer would be interested in working with PSTA to provide free transportation as a benefit! Click here to learn more about fares and our fare programs. Commuter Service Have a group at work that would be interested in carpooling? PSTA’s Vanpool might be the perfect solution for you. The Vanpool program lets you lease an Enterprise vehicle to share with 4 to 15 other commuters, helping you save on gas, avoid daily wear and tear on your personal vehicle, and reduce the time y … th 26 locations throughout the county, Direct Connect makes it easier and more affordable to connect to bus service. How PSTA Remains Steady Amidst Fuel Uncertainty Unlike the average fuel consumer, PSTA locks in its diesel prices at the beginning of the fiscal year. This allows PSTA to continue providing service regardless of the price per barrel. But there’s another reason PSTA is resilient to soaring gas prices—81.9% of our fleet is either full-electric or hybrid-electric buses. A GILLIG electric bus charging at PSTA’s headquarters. Our hybrid-electric buses use far less fuel than our 40 di …  our 40 diesel buses, and our all-electric vehicles, of course, use no fuel at all and can travel up to 300 miles on a single charge. With a fleet less dependent on diesel and the agency’s fuel prices locked in for the year, PSTA is uniquely positioned to weather any fuel pricing storm that comes our way—and we want to share those benefits with YOU! Historically, we see ridership increase when gas prices go up. In fact, data show that a 10% sustained rise in gas prices leads to a 4% to 9% jump in ridership—and PSTA is ready for this, as we always are. Properly dispose of trash No animals except service animals No soliciting or selling goods Do not play music through external speakers Shirt and sho … or emergency exits. Limit personal items. Do not bring shopiping carts on board. Do not hang from handrails or straps and do not place your feet on the seats. Use appropriate language and content in conversations. Do not obstruct, hinder or interfere with streetcar operators or other passengers. SAFETY IS OUR #1 PRIORITY Additional Safety Tips KEEP THE QLINE MOVING SAFELY Stay inside the white traffic lines when parking. Do not park or idle on the streetcar tracks. Leave extra space when parking near corners and driveways. Double check your parking before walking away. Obey all posted signs an … k your parking before walking away. Obey all posted signs and traffic laws along the streetcar route. Parking Safety Park & Ride Improper parking can delay QLINE service by an average of 27 minutes and it could result in your vehicle being towed. BIKES, SCOOTERS & STROLLERS Bikes, strollers and personal scooters are allowed on the qline, space permitting, and must be stored in the center section of the streetcar. Bikes should be stored upright on a hanging rack. Micromobility rideshare options, such as Mogo, Lime, Bird, Spin, and others are not permitted on the QLINE. Streetcar stations should … t on a hanging rack. Micromobility rideshare options, such as Mogo, Lime, Bird, Spin, and others are not permitted on the QLINE. Streetcar stations should not be used for bike storage. RIDE SMART, STAY SAFE Cross the tracks at a 90-degree angle when riding a bike or scooter. Use the hanging hooks to hold your bike when riding the streetcar. Look both ways before crossing. An art contest inviting young artists across Santa Clara County to imagine where VTA can take them next. VTA’s teamed up with three incredible local institutions, the Children's Discovery Museum, The Tech Interactive, and the San José Museum of Art, to turn imagination into real, rideable art throughout the community. Young artists will submit their artwork, and the chosen pieces will end up on VTA vehicles or transit stops to be seen by thousands of riders. The Theme Next Stop: Imagination! Think about your own rides on the bus or light rail. Who do you see? Where do you go? How  … sibilities?
